questions.prompt: Use a 30°-60°-90° triangle with hypotenuse 1 to derive sin(π/3) and cos(π/3).
questions.prompt_markup: Use a 30°-60°-90° triangle with hypotenuse 1 to derive sin(π/3) and cos(π/3).
questions.correct_answer: Halving an equilateral triangle gives legs 1/2 and √(1 - 1/4) = √3/2; the angle π/3 is opposite √3/2, so sin(π/3) = √3/2 and cos(π/3) = 1/2.
questions.required_method: Start from an equilateral triangle of side 1 cut in half.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof or derivation. Essential: the half-equilateral triangle, the Pythagorean Theorem, and the ratio.
